findings.what: The runtime module's header comment claims the reason set is 'that same five plus ONE the new door introduces — `core_unreadable`, D16's required-read arm', and `retrieveKnowledge` branches on `answer.core_readable !== false` to produce a `core_unreadable` reason. But migration 0230's `clara.retrieve_knowledge` (packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:265-413) never emits a `core_readable`/`core_readable:false` field in its returned jsonb (grep for `core_readable` across the whole migration file returns zero hits) — confirmed by reading the full function body and by `grep -n "core_readable" packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql` returning nothing. The SQL door is one atomic SELECT, so it cannot independently fail on the core tier while the rest succeeds; any failure (lock timeout, refusal, etc.) already throws and is caught by the existing try/catch, landing on `refused`/`read_failed`/`malformed` (all of which already map to `denied`/`unknown` through `faceStatusOf`, satisfying D16's 'if the core cannot be read the whole answer is unavailable' by construction). The `core_readable`/`core_unreadable`/`core_ok` code path is therefore dead code against the real production door: it is exercised only by test `kr.07` (knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs:133-141), which fabricates a synthetic answer object `{ ...ANSWER, core_readable: false }` that `retrieve_knowledge` can never actually produce. This does not cause incorrect behaviour today (the atomic door already yields the D16-correct outcome through the ordinary failure paths), and the final report correctly labels the D16 terminal as 'contract-only', but the comment overclaims what the door does and the test gives false confidence that a real door capability was exercised.
findings.failure_scenario: A future implementer (e.g. at the claraWork_v5 cut) reads the `core_unreadable` branch and its test and concludes the SQL door already distinguishes 'core failed' from 'everything failed', then designs the v5 required-read terminal assuming that signal exists and is meaningful, when in fact it will never fire from the real door as built — wasted design/debugging time, or a false sense that D16's core-tier distinction is more granular than it actually is.
findings.fix: Either (a) correct the comment to state plainly that the door is atomic and cannot signal a core-only failure today, so `core_readable` is speculative/defensive code with no live producer, and drop or clearly mark `kr.07` as testing a hypothetical future door shape rather than current behaviour; or (b) remove the dead `core_readable` branch entirely until a future migration actually needs to distinguish tier-level failure, relying instead on the already-correct fact that any door exception already yields `unknown`/`denied` (which is sufficient for D16 given the door's current atomic shape).
